recentItems.title: Cyprus attorney general rejects bid to drop case of UK boy’s fatal fall
recentItems.description:
(17 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Paphos, Cyprus - 17 September 2026
1. Wide of Paphos court
2. Lettering on building identifying court
3. Wide of EU and Cypriot flags
4. Various of police van on side of building
5. Wide of courthouse exterior
6. British man's lawyer, Alexandros Alexandrou, speaking on phone outside courthouse
7. Lettering on building identifying court
8. SOUNDBITE (English) Alexandros Alexandrou, British man's lawyer:
"We have asked for more time, a couple of days, just to explain the procedure. As you all saw, he's not in a good condition; he's not understanding very well our procedures in our criminal producer. That's why I need him to relax from this tension he's living while he's inside the courtroom: to explain quietly which facts he has against, which facts he has in his favor, to understand how it's going to continue this procedure in case he will plead not guilty." 
9. Mid of vehicles outside courthouse
10. SOUNDBITE (English) Alexandros Alexandrou, British man's lawyer:
"The major issues are that he will be forced to be in the court during all the evidence shown to him, to recalling in his memory all the tragic facts that he had lived that day, and I need to explain to him which evidence we will be presenting to him and what are the consequences in each plea."
11. Wide of vehicles outside courthouse
12. SOUNDBITE (English) Alexandros Alexandrou, British man's lawyer:
(reacting after the country's top lawyer denied a request to dismiss the case on humanitarian grounds)
"I express surprise because it was something that in my state of mind, it's something that is very different and it is different from other cases that, (pauses) I would prefer not to go further."
13. People walking outside courthouse
14. SOUNDBITE (English) Alexandros Alexandrou, British man's lawyer:
(answering media question regarding whether he and his client are considering a plea deal)
"We didn't get into this kind of conversation, because as I have explained before, in order to consider myself as a professional, I need to explain him and to be confident that he understood what I was telling him. He's not in a very good state of mind by the meaning to understand the procedure."
15. People outside courthouse
16. SOUNDBITE (English) Alexandros Alexandrou, British man's lawyer:
"Yesterday was his son's birthday. He was here, his wife (isn't here). He's in a bad condition. His daughter as well. They need him. They need him, and he needs them as well."
17. People outside courthouse
18. Wide of gate to courthouse grounds
STORYLINE:
The lawyer for a British man charged with negligence in the falling death of his 3-year-old son from a Cyprus hotel window said Thursday his client was disappointed that the attorney general denied a request to dismiss the case on humanitarian grounds.

The 37-year-old defendant, who authorities haven’t named publicly, was accompanied by his parents to court Thursday in the coastal resort town of Paphos. He was due to plead to a single charge of causing death due to negligent and careless actions. But Judge Froso Christodoulides granted his request to postpone proceedings until Tuesday. 

Lawyer Alexandros Alexandrou said he was surprised that Attorney General George Savvides denied the request to dismiss the case. 

State prosecutors told the court that although the attorney general understands the defendant's grief, the case must proceed as a matter of public interest.


The circumstances of the fall remain unclear.




AP Video and production by Menelaos Hadjicostis

recentItems.title: Hip hop star Travis McCoy on his HIV awareness film and record
recentItems.description:
(28 Apr 2011) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, November 9th 2009
10 mins approx
1. Sit down interview with Travis McCoy including the following sound bites:
"When I was younger I had someone very close to me die from AIDS and, so if there''s any charity or campaign that I''d want to back, if I had some extra time away from touring and Gym Class Heroes and everything, it was definitely Staying Alive. So we built, I built a relationship with Georgia over a little bit of time after the EMA''s and I was just like ''what else can I do?'' and she was like ''well there''s a lot you can do'' and I was like ''throw it at me'' and then we started talking about taking this trip and what not and the rest is history."
"There''s such a sense of community in every country that I visited that they were just so welcoming and so open to share culturally and what they were doing as far as raising awareness and education and all that, I just felt a part of something."
"Having clean water to drink, just waking up and not having to walk for miles to fill jugs of water just to shower just to wash yourself. All these small things I definitely took for granted before this trip and now it''s like I wake up every morning so grateful."
"Shortly after I got home I found a YouTube video of a kid whose mother had cancelled his subscription to the World of War Craft and he flipped out like he ran to his room, tore his clothes off screamed ''I want to die, I don''t want to live'', it was like wow my theory rang true these kids don''t realise how good they actually have it. If I had it in my power to take that kid and drop him off in Kalicha, what would he do without internet or without video games, he''d probably go crazy."
"Aside from the fact I promised Staying Alive that I''d raise at least £100,000 for the charity through this song, it''s up for download on World AIDS day which is December 1st and all the proceeds from iTunes go directly back to Staying Alive. So I had that pressure and then I had the pressure of keeping my artistic integrity and keeping the cheese factor at a bare minimum because you want the song to appeal to, not just one particular demographic, you want it to appeal to everyone."
"I''m proud of it, I''m proud of this song and now we have to wait to December 1st to see if I can come through on my promise."

recentItems.title: Man of Steel Premiere
recentItems.description:
(12 Jun 2013) 
AP Entertainment
London, 12 June 2013
1. Wide exterior shot of blue carpet
2. Wide shot of fans waiting
3. Medium shot of young fan in Superman costume
4. Medium shot of Henry Cavill arriving
5. Medium shot of Michael Shannon arriving
6. Close up of Henry Cavill talking to reporter
7. SOUNDBITE (English) Henry Cavill, Actor:
(Reporter: "You must miss this weather - the British summertime - when you're out in California")
"You know what? I do. California is great and all and it's nice to have nice sunny weather but this is home, so it's different."
8. Pull out from Superman logo to fans
9. SOUNDBITE (English) Amy Adams, Actress:
"It's really great. I've had such wonderful memories in London and it's always fun to come and get to celebrate film here. I mean look at the turnout. It's amazing. Overwhelming."
10. Close up Michael Shannon speaking to reporters
11. SOUNDBITE (English) Michael Shannon, Actor: 
"It's amazing. I went to a theater on the West End, the Vaudeville Theatre on The Strand today, where I did a play like 18 years ago. I hadn't been back there in 18 years. I walked in the lobby, asked if I could look inside because I was feeling a little nostalgic and it's just fascinating to think about everything that's happened between then and now."
Warner Bros.
12. Trailer clip, "Man of Steel" trailer
AP Entertainment
London, 12 June 2013
13. SOUNDBITE (English) Zack Snyder, Director:
"I don't know. We were talking about the fact that maybe because those characters are so iconographically American in a weird way and maybe because those characters sort of talk about the culture and the world in general, then maybe because they're British they can actually - I think in the case of Superman, the case of Henry - he's able to kind of like create an American icon from an objective standpoint and not just have it baked into his own culture. It's interesting. Not that Superman isn't baked into British culture because he is a little bit."
14. SOUNDBITE (English) Amy Adams, Actress:
"You know I think that there's still this gentleman quality that's really respected over here and I think it adds an element to the superhero where you can bring a lot of masculinity and bravado, but at the same time you're gentleman and that comes across."
Warner Bros.
15. Trailer clip, "Man of Steel" trailer
AP Entertainment
London, 12 June 2013
16. Medium shot Michael Shannon speaking to reporters
17. SOUNDBITE (English) Michael Shannon, Actor: 
"We all kind of worked out together. Henry obviously worked out a lot harder than I did, but it was nice because it kind of established relationships before we started shooting. We got to know each other and you really get to know someone when you're sweating to death next to them. There's nowhere to hide so it was nice."
Reporter: "Any competition between you?"
Shannon: "No, no, no. We're so far apart it's not even funny."
18. Medium shot Henry Cavill talking to reporter
19. SOUNDBITE (English) Henry Cavill, Actor:
"It's always a bonding experience when you're working that hard and you know how much the other person's suffering and you're suffering as much. It took a lot of hard work on both of our parts to get in the crazy shape we did. Just constant training. It was five months of training before we started shooting and six months afterwards and yeah, it does create a bond."
Warner Bros.
20. Trailer clip, "Man of Steel" trailer
AP Entertainment
London, 12 June 2013
21. Close up of Russell Crowe talking to reporter
22. SOUNDBITE (English) Russell Crowe, Actor:
Warner Bros.
23. Trailer clip, "Man of Steel" trailer

recentItems.title: Elton John and David Furnish''s flamboyant clothing collection up for sale
recentItems.description:
(28 Apr 2011) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, December 8th 2009
10 mins approx
1. Close of shoes
2. Close of glittery boots
3. Various clothes
4. Photo call of David Furnish and models with leopard print bags
5. Various of models wearing items from the clothing collection
6. Interview with David Furnish including the following sound bites:
"This is our fourth ''Out the Closet'' event, and it sort of comes from a full clean-out of the wardrobes, going through, getting rid of just about everything except the stuff that you absolutely need to wear right now. It''s great for the fans because they get a piece of memorabilia, it''s wonderful for people who are fans and collectors of fashion because there''s a lot of fashion history here, and for someone who''s just looking for a bargain, like a nice overcoat or business suit. It''s an opportunity to get a beautifully made, beautifully detailed garment at a fraction of what you''d pay for it at the shops, and all of the money raised goes to support the Elton John Aids Foundation, so I kind of look at it as a win-win situation for everybody."
"It''s interesting when you go out into the field, and you see the way the money makes a difference, any hoarding mentality that you might have tends to kind of go out the window. But this sale, more in particular for me, actually both Elton and I are sort of at a point of change in our clothing sizes, I''ve gone up a jacket size, I had a spinal surgery two years ago that limited my ability to exercise and to gym and to train so I''ve gone up a jacket size so a lot of the pieces that I put in the sale I just can''t fit into them anymore, so a lot of beautiful size forty jackets, I can''t squeeze into them. Elton''s losing a lot of weight so there''s a lot of pieces that he doesn''t want to fit into anymore either, so it''s a whole cross section of different pieces and different sizes."
"We get sent a lot of things, designers send us clothing, or they give us items at discount prices, more things than we can ever possibly wear. It''s just great to clean it out, and to put it into the hands of people who love it and appreciate it and raise money for the charity."
7. Various of clothes
8. Various of hats
9. Various of shoes
10. Various exteriors of where the event is being held

recentItems.title: Singer talks about her new album and tour
recentItems.description:
(28 Apr 2011) 

STORYLINE:
SHOTLIST
London, August 25th 2009
10 mins approx
1. Sit down interview with Beverley Knight including the following sound bites: 
On her new album:
"Yeah, it''s about all things new with a new and happy relationship and certainly love and also a nod to the past and where I''d been, but placing it in the past, firmly there. It''s just a whole new exciting era."
On the single ''Beautiful Night'':
"Once Amanda, Amanda Ghost who I co-wrote it with, once we''d finished the writing and it was literally just herself and myself and the guitar at first, that''s all we had, and just sang the songs through, we were like (nods) this sounds great as it is, the song stands up. Once she brought in The Rural, who are a production outfit that she''s been working with for a long time, they did what they do. It was like, ''This is definitely a single. Definitely the lead off single''."
"I really enjoyed doing it, I had to learn a few of the moves which terrified me, really terrified me. There was Jason and Tanisha, actually were the dancers and then I was swapping with Tanisha and doing some of those moves as well. It was great, it was really great." 
"This record just flowed... The process was so fluid, everything connected up, one thing led to another which led to another experience and by the time I''d finished it was like, ''Oh yeah, the album''s written now, great.''"
"Well the tour is the absolute epicentre, the nucleus of everything I do, it''s the most important part of my musical life and I''ll be showcasing heavily from ''100%'', the album. But I''ll totally be going right back to the beginning and pulling out all the songs that got me to the place where I stand today and to just remind people of the journey that I''ve been on and that they''ve helped me to go on as well. So a mixture of old and new."
